title: Read a short bean plant study
objective: Find the main idea, check a detail, and spot a claim the text cannot support.
context: A class compared 30 bean plants. Each group had 10 plants. One group had 8 hours of light a day. The other groups had 4 hours or no light. All plants got the same amount of water. After 14 days, the 8-hour group was the tallest on average (18 cm). This classroom passage gives no heights for the other groups.

items.prompt: Read once. What question did the class ask?
items.answer: 2 marks: asks about daily light (1) and the height or growth of bean plants (1). Accept a clear question in the student’s own words.
items.hint: What did the class change? What did it measure?

items.prompt: Find three details: the number of plants in each group, the length of the study, and the mean height of the tallest group.
items.answer: 1 mark each: 10 plants per group, 14 days, 18 cm. Do not accept 30 as the group size.
items.hint: Read the words around each number.

items.prompt: A reader says the 8-hour group was twice as tall as the 4-hour group. Can you check this? Explain.
items.answer: We cannot check it (1). We need the mean height of the 4-hour group (1).
items.hint: Which two heights would you need?

items.prompt: Write one sentence that reports the main result. Include a group, a number, and its unit.
items.answer: Example: After 14 days, the 8-hour group was tallest, with a mean height of 18 cm. Give 1 mark for the correct group, 1 for the comparison and 1 for 18 cm as a mean.
items.hint: In this class study, the ___ group …

slides.title: Read for the main idea
body: With a partner, name the thing the class changed and the thing it measured.

slides.title: Scan for a detail
body: Scan means to look quickly for one detail.
Underline the words around each number. What does each number describe?

slides.title: Check a claim
body: Find the two values you would need to check it. Are both in the text?

slides.title: Write and check
body: Write one result in your own words.
Ask a partner to check your group, number, and unit against the passage.
